root_cause.text: In qfq_reset_qdisc, the code incorrectly uses the shared leaf qdisc's queue length (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0) as a proxy for class activity, which can falsely trigger deactivation of an inactive aggregate when multiple QFQ classes share the same leaf qdisc, leading to a null pointer dereference in qfq_deactivate_agg.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0)` to `if (cl_is_active(cl))`. The commit message states that two qfq_class objects may point to the same leaf_qdisc, causing the leaf_qdisc's qlen to be >0 due to enqueues through a different QFQ qdisc, and the qfq_reset would wrongly deactivate an inactive aggregate, triggering the null-deref. The crash trace confirms the null deref at qfq_deactivate_agg.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix QFQ class deactivation during Qdisc reset by using cl_is_active() instead of queue length check to correctly handle active classes with no pending packets.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in qfq_reset_qdisc from checking if the class's qdisc queue length is greater than zero (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0) to calling cl_is_active(cl) to determine whether to deactivate the class.
intent_record.how: This change alters the behavior during Qdisc reset: instead of deactivating a class only when its queue has packets, it now deactivates a class if it is considered active, which may include classes that are scheduled but have an empty queue. This ensures that all active classes are properly deactivated during reset.
